properties.title: Embedding Fear in Medical AI: A Risk-Averse Framework for Safety and Ethics
Embedding Fear in Medical AI: A Risk-Averse Framework for Safety and Ethics

assertions.rationale: Clinical inputs are examples; no variable-level provenance or transformation pipeline is specified.
No dataset or retained acquisition/event timestamp format is supplied.
Continuous incoming data are envisioned, but availability versus collection time is unspecified.
Sparse inputs are discussed through cited work; this proposal defines no missing/invalid mask.
No elapsed-since-measurement representation is specified for the proposed module.
No temporal integration or irregular event processing algorithm is given.
Requesting additional input is discussed without a model of observation occurrence.

assertions.applicability_reason: The conceptual proposal preprocesses no observed dataset; a witness-preservation audit has no performed pipeline target.

assertions.rationale: Imaging, laboratory and clinical data examples have no source-to-target semantic/unit mapping.

assertions.applicability_reason: No training dataset, splits or fitted preprocessing exist in this theoretical framework.

assertions.rationale: No cross-site federation protocol or exchanged training artifacts are specified.
The knowledge component gathers information without an operational observation-to-state mapping.
LLMs and image classifiers are cited context; no pretrained checkpoint is reused by a proposed implementation.
No context-to-target latent objective is defined; RL penalties concern action risk.

assertions.applicability_reason: No predictive latent representation objective is instantiated for collapse control.

assertions.rationale: The paper defines no observation reconstruction loss.
Multiple clinical inputs feed a schematic, with no specified fusion operator.
No modality-quality/availability-conditioned fusion behavior is specified.
Error memory and feedback are proposed, but no defined patient/scene state carried through prediction is operationalized.
Bayesian adverse-event probabilities are not a specified posterior over evolving hidden patient state.
Bayesian updating is described generally; separate state propagation/correction operations are not defined.
New data update risk estimates in the concept, without a defined individual state assimilation mechanism.
Weight/threshold adjustment is suggested, but no patient-specific fitting rule is supplied.
The framework targets varied uses without a shared learned state/checkpoint across typed tasks.

assertions.applicability_reason: No implemented state representation exists to ablate or test for predictive sufficiency.

assertions.rationale: Past errors affect caution conceptually; individual patient observation/action history conditioning is unspecified.

assertions.applicability_reason: No patient-specific model or forecast is evaluated, so history-swap tests have no model target.

assertions.rationale: No patient/anatomical identity consistency mechanism through transitions is specified.
Explaining risk alerts is proposed rather than a mapping from state coordinates to physiology.
Past-mistake memory is specified as a role, without storage/retrieval form or history extent.
Surgery/drug recommendations are examples; no separated settable action query to a prediction model is specified.
Treatment and further-input examples are not a formal role/effect-channel schema.
No executable action dose, route, duration, unit or robot frame is supplied.
No time-indexed intervention schedule or cadence is defined.
No semantics for joint treatment or inherited settings are supplied.
Risk thresholds and RL penalties do not define a context-specific feasible candidate set.
Illustrated clinical actions lack an operational variable-to-execution mapping.
No historical overlap/support estimate is performed for proposed choices.

assertions.applicability_reason: This paper reports no same-origin alternative-action prediction experiment.

assertions.rationale: Harmful incision/delay and human liability are discussed; residual/reversibility analysis of specified actions is missing.
Planning/feedback boxes do not define a state transition over a health-world coordinate.
RL learning is suggested, but no learned or identified health-state transition is specified.
No transition consumes specified treatments; risk assessment examples do not establish it.
GP/dropout/Bayesian risk estimates do not define a random next-state process.
Amygdala analogy is not a physiological law constraining health-state transition.
Biological analogy plus RL does not operationally couple mechanistic and learned dynamics.
No exchangeable dynamics implementations or state/action contract is provided.
Medical and military examples do not exchange state across biological scales.
No optimization through predicted health-state transitions is specified.
Hierarchical human override does not define variable-duration world transitions.
Diagnosis/recommendation arrows are not a specified emission mapping from internal state.
Risk/benefit inputs to utility have no learned typed outcome heads or horizons.

assertions.applicability_reason: The conceptual paper has no implemented model or successor-state experiment.

assertions.rationale: Strategy simulation is proposed without successive generated-state transitions.

assertions.applicability_reason: There is no evaluated prediction sequence with intermediate conditioning.

assertions.rationale: Monitoring feedback is proposed without an imagined/executed state and measured correction protocol.

assertions.applicability_reason: No prediction experiment is conducted, hence no furthest tested horizon.
No free-running forecast exists for depth-dependent error testing.
No forecast curve/tolerance exists for a validated horizon.

assertions.rationale: Uncertainty methods are suggested without coherent conditional trajectory sampling.
No supported prediction horizon or out-of-horizon response policy is specified.
Planning/prediction simulates strategies and sends risk signals in a conceptual flow; actual simulator and coupling are unspecified.
PPO and risk-sensitive policies are suggestions without operational model-coupled search/policy.
Feedback loop has no execution prefix or stated recomputed planning horizon.
Adjustable utility weights do not establish fixed learned dynamics reusable across objectives.
The proposed utility includes UQ and high uncertainty changes escalation/acceptance; this is specification, not tested safety.

assertions.applicability_reason: No optimized model-coupled plans are evaluated to test exploitation of model error.

assertions.rationale: No candidate set or future-independent construction/coverage protocol is defined.
Chief-doctor supervision is not a higher/lower-level option policy with model use.

assertions.applicability_reason: The monitoring/execution cycle is a proposal; no environment interaction experiment is run.

assertions.rationale: Bayesian harm probabilities and GP/dropout uncertainty are named with decision roles; estimator/distribution configuration is missing.
criteria_met: named Bayesian/GP/dropout methods and harm-risk semantics

assertions.rationale: No aleatoric/epistemic decomposition procedure or semantics are supplied.

assertions.applicability_reason: Threshold tuning on historical/simulated cases is future work; no empirical calibration sample/result exists.
No trajectory prediction is implemented/evaluated for path reliability.
No performed calibration protocol or acceptance tolerance exists.

assertions.rationale: Anomaly detection is proposed as a defense without statistic/threshold/detection result.
No nonconformity score, calibration split or coverage assumptions are supplied.

assertions.applicability_reason: The proposal supplies no causal treatment contrast or empirical effect estimand.
No causal effect is estimated by the proposed framework.
There is no identified causal estimand requiring exchangeability/positivity assumptions.
No causal estimate or identification assumptions are analyzed.
No action-effect predictions or interventional ground-truth experiment are reported.

assertions.rationale: Risk examples provide no calibrated intervention-to-physiology mechanism.

assertions.applicability_reason: Anticipated safer care is not an estimated treatment effect with identification/validation.

assertions.rationale: Soft RL penalties and proposed pauses are not an implemented blocker with tested fail behavior.
Proposed high-risk/uncertain decisions are withheld pending human review, with safe low-risk support fallback.
Physician role and continued safe support are proposed; availability and response-time guarantees remain unspecified.
Proposed continuous risk/uncertainty signals trigger pauses/escalation; sensitivity and latency remain untested.
Pausing and maintaining current treatment are proposed; physical residual effects and stop/fallback tests are missing.
Poisoned/spoofed sensor readings and false-alarm/masked-risk attack paths are analyzed; full state/action/rollout interface coverage is missing.

assertions.applicability_reason: Adversarial exposure is a suggested future training method, not an attack/fault evaluation.

assertions.rationale: No operational de-identification, access or privacy-control mechanism is specified.

assertions.applicability_reason: No trained generator or representation outputs exist for disclosure testing.

assertions.rationale: Human decision authority is asserted without external-system permission enforcement.
Alert explanation and human override are proposed; interface protocol and measured human factors are not established.
Medical decision support and clinician authority are described using radiology/ICU/surgery examples; population and bounded operating context remain broad.

assertions.applicability_reason: No implemented versioned model or asset exists for a model-card report.

assertions.rationale: Monitoring/feedback and logs are proposed; released-use cadence, owner and revalidation triggers are not specified.
Learning/adjustment box gives no versioned update approval, rollback or revalidation rules.
FDA is named as an anticipated regulator; this is mention, not applicability or authorization.

assertions.applicability_reason: The framework is theoretical and future certification is recommended; no product/use authorization is claimed.
Authors explicitly state IRB and informed consent are not applicable to this conceptual study.

assertions.rationale: Proposed agent knowledge/planning/execution/monitoring roles are described; no actual operative agent is implemented.
Future training with AI plus human-like overseer is proposed; communication and coordination protocol is not specified.
Proposed feedback updates plans/knowledge; a defined implemented agent revision procedure is missing.
No operational external API/tool invocation or read/write scope is provided.
Physician final authority and safe autonomous support are proposed; operational execution/approval boundary is not tested or bounded.
No code release is identified; data-availability statement directs inquiries to corresponding author.

assertions.applicability_reason: No model is trained, hence no trained weights are an output of this study.
Article CC BY is visible but there is no code/weights/data asset to which this feature applies.
There is no empirical implementation/result for an independent reproduction.
No successor-state prediction model or experiment exists in this conceptual study.
No free-running/block future-sequence experiment is conducted.
No generated distribution is compared with reference samples.
Illustrative aneurysm/triage scenarios are not a plausibility or constraint experiment.
Risk thresholds are proposed without held-out calibration or coverage results.
No controlled action-input sensitivity experiment exists.
No intervention/counterfactual validation experiment exists.
No individualized forecast model is tested with history controls.
No operative model-coupled decision policy or decision endpoint is evaluated.
No matched simulation/physical or clinical execution experiment exists.
No model/data evaluation exists for independent-cohort, shift or subgroup testing.
No processed measurements/grid are tested for witness preservation.
Cited surveys and anticipated clinician oversight are not an actual review/use study of this module.
Latency/load concerns are qualitative future engineering needs; no computational experiment exists.
The authors explicitly report no empirical/clinical trial validation; anticipated patient safety is untested.

assertions.rationale: No evolving internal representation transition is defined; deep fear-layer imagery is conceptual.
Fear penalties shape a suggested RL objective without learned transition states or value-equivalence contract.

relation_assertions.rationale: Reviewer synthesis: proposed risk/uncertainty escalation and threat analysis inform safety responsibility.
Reviewer synthesis: human authority, explanation/logging and future governance inform lifecycle responsibility.

legacy_cells.B: Embedding Fear in Medical AI: A Risk-Averse Framework for Safety and Ethics
legacy_cells.I: 013_2025_Embedding Fear in Medical AI A Risk-Averse Framework for Safety and Ethics.pdf
legacy_cells.EN: Discusses poisoning attacks and spoofed inputs as threats; proposes independent input checks, anomaly detection, and robust learning as countermeasures, without testing them.
legacy_cells.FL: Conceptual architecture: knowledge, planning/prediction, amygdala-like risk evaluator, execution, monitoring/feedback, and learning/adjustment components; no implemented encoder, persistent state, or learned transition is specified.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes a medical-AI caution/fear framework combining Bayesian adverse-outcome risk estimates, reinforcement-learning penalties for harmful choices, uncertainty assessment, memory of errors, and human oversight.
legacy_cells.FN: No empirical findings; the paper states there is no direct evidence that an AI with an embedded fear module outperforms one without it.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state the framework is conceptual and unvalidated empirically or in clinical trials; accurate risk probabilities are assumed, applicability may vary, and implementation costs/data/regulatory needs are not fully addressed.
legacy_cells.FP: Calls for empirical calibration of fear thresholds and evaluation in live or simulated high-stakes settings, including clinical trials or sandbox testing.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify a lack of direct evidence and prior direct exploration of an embedded fear module for patient safety in AI.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence boundary: the paper proposes mechanisms and workflows but demonstrates no implemented transition model, rollout, comparative performance, safety benefit, or clinical outcome.
legacy_cells.FT: Represent risk and uncertainty with explicit thresholds that trigger human review rather than an outright veto, and calibrate thresholds to context.
legacy_cells.FX: Read the complete extracted 33-page PDF stream: title page and abstract (p. 1); Introduction (pp. 1–4); conceptual foundations and architecture proposal (pp. 4–19); practical considerations and implementation approaches (pp. 18–21); counterarguments/security discussion (pp. 21–24); broader implications, open questions, limitations, and conclusion (pp. 24–28); Tables 1–3 and publication/data/ethics statements (pp. 5, 18, 25–28); references through p. 33. No empirical Methods/Results experiment section is reported. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I were left untouched as instructed; metadata is context only. The paper explicitly describes the proposal as theoretical and unvalidated, so no demonstrated world-model capability or clinical readiness beyond R0 is supported. Extracted figure/table layout is OCR-corrupted in places (notably pp. 16–18); this does not alter the conceptual/no-empirical-evaluation determination. The supplied files do not include the blueprint codebook, so FS/FU give generic evidence-backed mappings without module/open-problem IDs. Evidence QA: 11/20 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (55%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 17 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 3 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Conceptual framework only; no model implementation, empirical evaluation, patient benefit or validated safety thresholds.
Paper contains extensive cited examples; none are attributed as experiments of the proposed module.
Utility-sign/threshold direction is ambiguous; positive risk coefficient and below-threshold escalation require clarification before implementation.
PDF embeds figure screenshots with duplicate underlying text and different internal pagination; citations use physical pages.
No independent human entailment review or external code/supplement inspection was performed.
notes: Source read in full (physical pp1–33), references included; all 6 figures and 3 tables visually checked. No appendix or separate supplement identified. Proposed safety architecture informs M9/M10 only at specification/claim stage.
